scenes.vo: An old man in our market sold empty glass jars. The label said: patience. Ten rupees.
scenes.cap: An old man sold empty jars labelled "Patience". ₹10 each.

scenes.vo: Everyone laughed. Ten rupees for nothing? But one boy bought a jar, just to prove him wrong.
scenes.cap: Everyone laughed. One boy bought a jar to prove him wrong.

scenes.vo: On the lid, a rule. Drop in one coin every day you don't lose your temper. Open it after one year.
scenes.cap: The rule: one coin for every day you don't lose your temper.

scenes.vo: The first week, the jar stayed empty. By the third month, he was winning most days. And something else changed. People started talking to him.
scenes.cap: Week 1: empty. Month 3: winning most days.

scenes.vo: A year later, the jar was full. He ran back to the old man. Was the patience in the coins?
scenes.cap: One year later, the jar was full.

scenes.vo: The old man smiled. The patience was never in the jar. I only sold you a reason to notice it. He still sells empty jars. Want one?
scenes.cap: "The patience was never in the jar." Want one?
